paragraphs: Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc., a Delaware corporation, together with its subsidiaries ("Chipotle," "we," "us," or "our") owns and operates Chipotle Mexican Grill restaurants, which feature a relevant menu of burritos, burrito bowls (a burrito without the tortilla), quesadillas, tacos, and salads. We strive to cultivate a better world by serving responsibly sourced, classically cooked, real food with wholesome ingredients and without artificial colors, flavors or preservatives. We are passionate about providing a great guest experience and making our food more accessible to everyone while continuing to be a brand with a demonstrated purpose. Our first Chipotle restaurant opened in Denver, Colorado in 1993. Over 30 years later, our devotion to seeking out high-quality ingredients, raised with respect for animals, farmers, and the environment, remains at the core of our commitment to Food with Integrity.

As of December 31, 2025, we owned 3,938 Chipotle restaurants throughout the United States ("U.S.") and 104 international Chipotle restaurants. Additionally, we had 14 international partner-operated restaurants. Partner-operated restaurants represent Chipotle restaurants over which Chipotle does not have a controlling financial interest and for which Chipotle does not directly manage day-to-day operations. This includes restaurants operated by third parties pursuant to license or franchise agreements and restaurants in which Chipotle holds a minority, non-controlling ownership interest. We manage our U.S. operations based on 11 regions and aggregate our operations to one reportable segment. Our revenue is derived from sales by our restaurants.

Chipotle is a brand with a demonstrated purpose of Cultivating a Better World. Our Recipe for Growth strategy leans into what uniquely differentiates Chipotle, with a focus on accelerating growth and sharpening competitiveness. The strategy is grounded in five key areas:
•Protect and strengthen the core by driving operational and culinary excellence to deliver exceptional value for our guests;
•Evolve the brand messaging and accelerate menu innovation and new occasions that drive demand into our restaurants;
•Modernize our business model with industry-leading technology, including leveraging AI and relaunching our Rewards Program, to elevate the experience for our guests and teams;
•Expand our global reach by scaling with intention through proven, company-owned and partner operated markets, as well as strategic new regions; and
•Cultivate the best talent in the industry that is energized and focused on speed and agility.

Serving high-quality food at reasonable prices is critical to ensuring guests enjoy wholesome food at a great value. In Chipotle-owned restaurants, we strive to serve only animal products that are raised in accordance with criteria we have established to improve sustainability and promote animal welfare, and without the use of non-therapeutic antibiotics or added growth hormones. We brand our meats as "Responsibly Raised®." We also seek to use responsibly grown produce, by which we mean produce grown by suppliers whose practices conform to our Food with Integrity standards and our priorities with respect to environmental considerations and employee welfare. For more information about our sustainability and animal welfare initiatives, see our biennial Sustainability Report and interim Update Report on our website www.chipotle.com/sustainability.

Maintaining the high levels of quality and safety we demand in our restaurants depends in part on our ability to acquire high-quality, fresh ingredients and other necessary supplies that meet our specifications from reliable suppliers. We work with multiple independently owned and operated regional distribution centers that purchase from various suppliers we carefully select based on the suppliers' understanding of and adherence to our mission and Food with Integrity standards, quality and price availability. We have also sought to increase the number of suppliers for our ingredients to help mitigate pricing volatility and reduce our reliance on one or several suppliers, which could create supply shortages. In addition, we closely monitor industry news, trade tariffs, weather, exchange rates, foreign demand, geopolitical crises and other world events that may affect our ingredient prices or available supply. Certain key ingredients are purchased from a small number of suppliers.

We are committed to serving only safe, high-quality food. Our food safety and quality assurance teams work to ensure compliance with our food safety programs and practices, components of which include:
•naturally derived inhibitors to prevent microbial growth in ingredients;
•advanced technologies and tools that reduce or eliminate pathogens while maintaining food quality;
•enhanced restaurant procedures and protocols for handling ingredients and sanitizing surfaces in our restaurants;

headings: Risks Related to our Brand Reputation and Restaurant Operations
Food safety and food-borne illness concerns may have an adverse effect on our business by negatively impacting our brand, decreasing sales and increasing costs.
Failure to maintain the value and reputation of the Chipotle brand could negatively impact our financial results.
The restaurant industry is highly competitive. If we are not able to compete successfully, our business, financial condition and results of operations would be adversely affected.
Our use of third-party delivery services may not be profitable and substandard service may negatively impact our reputation.
If we are not able to hire, train and retain qualified restaurant employees and/or appropriately plan our workforce, our growth plan and profitability could be adversely affected.
If we fail to comply with applicable employment and labor laws and regulations, it could have a material, adverse impact on our business.
Increases in the cost of labor, including mandated minimum wage increases and increases in the cost of health benefits, could adversely impact our business and profitability.
Risks Related to Cybersecurity, Data Privacy and IT Systems

We are heavily dependent on information technology systems and failures or interruptions in our IT systems could harm our ability to effectively operate our business and/or result in the loss of guests or employees.

If we fail to fully comply with privacy and data protection laws and regulations, we could incur significant civil and criminal penalties and liabilities, suffer reputational damage, and adverse publicity.
Risks Related to Our Supply Chain
Increases in the costs of ingredients, restaurant equipment and other materials could adversely affect our financial results.
Shortages or interruptions in the supply of ingredients could adversely affect our operating results.
If our supply chain capacity does not expand to support our new restaurant growth, our long-term growth goals could be impaired or delayed.
We could be party to litigation or other legal proceedings that could adversely affect our business, results of operations and reputation.
Risks Related to Our Growth and Business Strategy
If we are unable to meet our new restaurant opening goals, or maintain the attractiveness of our existing restaurants, our profitability could suffer.
Our failure to effectively manage and support our growth could have a negative adverse effect on our business and financial results.

We are subject to evolving public disclosure obligations, including with respect to sustainability matters, which could expose us to numerous risks and could adversely affect our reputation and results of operations.
Climate change and volatile adverse weather conditions could adversely affect our restaurant sales or results of operations.
Our financial condition and results of operations have been, and may continue to be, adversely affected by a number of macroeconomic and other factors, many of which are largely outside our control.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the risks described below in addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including the "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations" section and the consolidated financial statements and related notes. If any of the risks and uncertainties described below occur or continue to occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations, and the trading price of our common stock could be materially and adversely affected. The risks and uncertainties described below are those that we have identified as material but are not the only risks and uncertainties we face. Our business is also subject to general risks and uncertainties that affect many other companies, including, but not limited to, overall economic and industry conditions. Additional risks not currently known to us or that we presently deem immaterial may arise or become material and may negatively impact our business, reputation, financial condition, results of operations or the trading price of our common stock.

Food safety is our top priority, and we dedicate significant resources to ensuring that our food products are safe; however, even strong preventative controls and interventions from farm to restaurant cannot completely eliminate food safety risks. Incidents of food-borne illnesses have occurred and may continue to occur in our and other restaurants resulting from the failure of restaurant employees to properly cook or maintain ingredients; employees or guests entering a restaurant while infected with communicable diseases; or contaminated ingredients resulting from the failure of a supplier, distributor or employee to execute food safety preventive controls. Although we monitor and audit compliance with our program, we cannot guarantee that every food item is safely and properly maintained from the start of the supply chain through guest consumption. Any report, legitimate or rumored, of food-borne illness caused by pathogens such as E. coli, hepatitis A, norovirus, listeria, Campylobacter, Clostridium perfringens or salmonella, or other food safety issues, such as food tampering, contamination or natural or foreign objects, at one of our restaurants could adversely affect our reputation and have a negative impact on our sales. In addition, instances of food-borne illness or food safety issues that occur solely at competitors' restaurants or at suppliers or distributors (even if we do not work with them) could result in negative publicity about the restaurant industry and adversely impact our sales. The occurrence of food-borne illnesses or food safety issues could also adversely affect the price and availability of affected ingredients, resulting in higher costs and lower margins.

We may have higher risk for food safety incidents than some of our competitors because we use fresh, unprocessed produce, handle raw chicken in our restaurants, rely on employees cooking with traditional methods and don't use artificial preservatives or frozen ingredients in our menu items. The risk of illnesses associated with our food also may increase due to our delivery and catering businesses, in which our food is transported, stored and/or served in conditions that are not under our control. All of these factors could have an adverse impact on our ability to attract and retain guests, which could in turn have a material adverse effect on our growth and profitability. In addition, real or perceived concerns about pervasive chemicals and substances in the U.S. food supply chain, such as phthalates, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances ("PFAS"), microplastics or heavy metals, have been the subject of increased regulatory scrutiny and lawsuits against us and other restaurant companies, which could impact consumers' confidence in the restaurant industry and reduce restaurant sales.

We built strong value in the Chipotle brand by serving delicious, high quality food, made fresh every day using responsibly sourced ingredients served in generous portions. Our continued success depends on maintaining this compelling brand value, which may be eroded by numerous factors, some of which are outside of our control. Incidents that could erode trust in our brand include actual or perceived food safety or food-borne illnesses; allegations of unethical or unprofessional behavior by employees and/or guests; privacy breaches or violations of privacy laws; safety-related incidents occurring in or around our restaurants; guest perceptions regarding smaller entrée portion sizes; or other events or incidents described in this risk factors section. The adverse impact of such incidents may be compounded by negative publicity, including through social or digital media, or if they result in litigation. Social media, video-sharing, networking, and gaming and messaging platforms dramatically increase the speed and reach at which negative publicity is disseminated, often before we have a meaningful opportunity to investigate, respond to and address an issue. Negative online postings or comments about us, including as a result of inaccurate, fictitious or malicious postings or media content, have in the past and could in the future magnify and prolong the adverse impact of any one incident and increase the damage to the value of our brand.

Additionally, consumer demand for our products and our brand value could diminish significantly if we, our employees or business partners fail to comply with applicable laws and regulations, take positions or actions that may be considered controversial, fail to deliver a consistently positive guest experience or fail to foster an inclusive and welcoming environment. In addition, we cannot ensure that our restaurant crew or business partners will not take actions that adversely affect our brand reputation and relevance.

The restaurant industry is highly competitive on factors such as taste, price, food quality and selection, customer service, brand reputation, digital engagement, advertising and promotional initiatives, and the location, attractiveness and maintenance of restaurants. We also compete with non-traditional market participants, such as "convenience meals" in the form of entrées, side dishes or meal preparation kits from grocery stores, meal kit delivery services, and "ghost" or "dark" kitchens, where meals are prepared at separate takeaway premises rather than a restaurant. Delivery aggregators and food delivery services, which provide consumers with convenient access to a broad range of competing restaurant chains and food retailers, particularly in urbanized areas, may direct potential customers to other restaurants based on paid placements, online reviews and other factors, and may form a closer relationship with our guests. Increased competition could have an adverse effect on our sales, profitability and development plans. If guest tastes or dietary preferences change, if our marketing efforts are unsuccessful, or if we are unable to compete successfully with other restaurant concepts, our business could be adversely affected.

As of December 31, 2025, we owned 3,938 Chipotle restaurants throughout the United States, and 104 international Chipotle restaurants. Additionally, we had 14 international partner-operated restaurants. We manage our U.S. operations based on 11 regions and aggregate our operations to one reportable segment.

Throughout "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" we discuss the following key operating metrics which we believe will drive our financial results and long-term growth model. We believe these metrics are useful to investors because management uses these metrics to assess the growth of our business and the effectiveness of our marketing and operational strategies:
•Comparable restaurant sales •Food, beverage, and packaging as a percentage of total revenue
•Labor as a percentage of total revenue •Occupancy as a percentage of total revenue •Other operating costs as a percentage of total revenue
•Total revenue increased 5.4% to $11.9 billion •Comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7%
•Diluted earnings per share was $1.14, a 2.7% increase from $1.11

Sales Trends. Comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025. The decrease is attributable to lower transactions of 2.9%, partially offset by a 1.2% increase in average check. Comparable restaurant sales represent the change in period-over-period total revenue for company-owned restaurants in operation for at least 13 full calendar months. Digital sales represented 36.7% of total food and beverage revenue. For 2026, management is anticipating comparable restaurant sales to be about flat.

Restaurant Development. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we opened 334 company-owned restaurants, which included 257 restaurants with a Chipotlane. We expect to open approximately 350 to 370 restaurants in 2026, which includes 10 to 15 international partner-operated restaurants. We expect around 80% of our new company-owned restaurants will include a Chipotlane.
Partner-Operated Restaurants. During the year ended December 31, 2025, 11 partner-operated restaurants were opened in the Middle East.

headings: 本公司智慧財產權及商標
paragraphs: Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc., 一間 Delaware 公司，連同其子公司（"Chipotle," "we," "us," 或 "our"）擁有並營運 Chipotle Mexican Grill 餐廳，其特色為提供包含墨西哥捲餅（burritos）、無玉米餅的捲餅碗（burrito bowls）、奶酪薄餅（quesadillas）、墨西哥卷餅（tacos）及沙拉等相關餐點。我們致力於透過提供來源可追溯、傳統烹調、真實食材且不含人工色素、風味或防腐劑的餐點，來培育更美好的世界。我們熱衷於提供優質的顧客體驗，並讓更多人能享用我們的餐點，同時持續維持一個具備明確使命的品牌。我們的第一間 Chipotle 餐廳於 1993 年在美國科羅拉多州丹佛市開幕。超過 30 年後，我們對尋找高品質食材、以尊重動物、農民及環境的方式飼養的承諾，仍為我們 Food with Integrity 的宗旨核心。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在美國（"U.S.") 運營 3,938 間 Chipotle 餐廳，並在國際上運營 104 間 Chipotle 餐廳。此外，我們還有 14 間國際合作夥伴營運的餐廳。合作夥伴營運的餐廳為 Chipotle 餐廳，Chipotle 並未對其擁有控制性財務權益，且未直接管理其日常營運。這包括由第三方根據授權或特許經營協議營運的餐廳，以及 Chipotle 持有少數、非控制性股權的餐廳。我們根據 11 個區域管理美國的營運，並將營運整併為一個應報告分部。我們的營業收入來自於我們餐廳的銷售額。
Chipotle 是一個具備明確使命的品牌，其使命為 Cultivating a Better World。我們的 Recipe for Growth 策略聚焦於 Chipotle 獨特的差異點，並以加速成長與強化競爭力為重點。此策略建立在五大關鍵領域：
• 保護並強化核心業務，透過推動營運與廚藝卓越，為顧客提供卓越價值；
• 改進品牌訊息，加速餐點創新與新場合的發展，以提升餐廳的客流量；
• 透過業界領先的科技，包括運用人工智能（AI）與重新推出忠誠度計畫，來提升顧客與團隊的體驗；
• 透過已驗證的公司自有與合作夥伴營運市場，以及戰略性新地區，擴展我們的全球影響力；以及
• 培養業界最佳的人才，使其具備動力與專注於速度與靈活性。

提供高品質且價格合理的餐點，是確保顧客能以優質價格享用健康食物的關鍵。在Chipotle自有的餐廳中，我們致力於僅提供符合我們所建立標準的動物性產品，以提升永續性並促進動物福利，且不使用非治療性抗生素或添加生長激素。我們將肉類品牌為『Responsibly Raised®』。我們也致力於使用 responsibly grown 的蔬果，即由符合我們 Food with Integrity 標準、並符合我們對環境考量及員工福利優先事項的供應商所生產的蔬果。如需瞭解我們的永續性與動物福利計畫，請參閱我們網站 www.chipotle.com/sustainability 上的年度永續報告及中期更新報告。

維持我們餐廳中對品質與安全的高標準，部分取決於我們能否從可靠供應商處取得符合我們規格的高品質、新鮮原料及其他必要用品。我們與多個獨立經營的區域配送中心合作，這些配送中心從我們精心挑選的供應商處進貨，這些供應商瞭解並遵循我們的使命及 Food with Integrity 標準，同時具備品質、價格與供應的可用性。我們也致力於增加原料供應商的數量，以協助緩解價格波動並降低對單一或多個供應商的依賴，這可能會導致原料短缺。此外，我們密切關注產業新聞、貿易關稅、天氣、匯率、外國需求、地緣政治危機及其他可能影響原料價格或供應的國際事件。某些關鍵原料是由少量供應商所購買。
我們致力於僅提供安全、高品質的餐點。我們的食品安全與品質保證團隊致力於確保符合我們的食品安全計畫與作法，其內容包括：
• 自然來源的抑制劑以防止原料中的微生物生長；
• 先進的科技與工具以減少或消除病原體，同時維持食物品質；
• 改進的餐廳作業程序與規範，以處理原料並清潔餐廳內的表面。

paragraphs: 您應配合我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，一併閱讀本節內容。本表單 10-K 的此部分一般討論 2025 年的項目及 2025 年與 2024 年的年對年比較。未包含於本表單 10-K 中的 2023 年項目及 2024 年與 2023 年的年對年比較，可於我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日結年度的年度報告表單 10-K 中「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」部分，第 II 項，第 7 項找到。本討論包含風險、不確定性與假設的向前看陳述，這些因素可能導致我們的結果與預期有重大差異。請參閱「向前看陳述的警示說明」。導致這種差異的因素包括於第 1A 項「風險因素」、第 7A 項「市場風險的量化與質化揭露」及其他處於本報告中所描述的內容。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在美國擁有 3,938 家 Chipotle 餐廳，以及 104 家國際 Chipotle 餐廳。此外，我們還有 14 家國際合作夥伴經營的餐廳。我們根據 11 個地區管理美國運營，並將運營統合為一個應報告分部。
在「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」中，我們討論以下關鍵營運指標，我們認為這些指標將驅動我們的財務結果與長期成長模式。我們認為這些指標對投資者是有用的，因為管理層使用這些指標來評估我們業務的成長與行銷及營運策略的成效：
• 同店銷售 • 食品、飲料及包裝佔總營業收入的百分比
• 人力成本佔總營業收入的百分比 • 租賃成本佔總營業收入的百分比 • 其他營運成本佔總營業收入的百分比
• 總營業收入增加 5.4% 至 119 億美元 • 同店銷售減少 1.7%
• 稀釋每股盈餘為 1.14 美元，較 1.11 美元增加 2.7%
銷售趨勢。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度，同店銷售減少 1.7%。減少的原因是交易量減少 2.9%，部分抵銷平均消費金額增加 1.2%。同店銷售代表公司擁有且營運至少 13 個完整曆月的餐廳，相鄰期間總營業收入的變化。數位銷售佔總食品與飲料營收的 36.7%。對於 2026 年，管理層預期同店銷售將大致維持不變。
餐廳開發。在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度內，我們開設了334家本公司所有餐廳，其中包括257家附設Chipotlane。我們預期在2026年將開設約350至370家餐廳，其中包括10至15家國際合作夥伴經營的餐廳。我們預期約80%的新本公司所有餐廳將附設Chipotlane。
合作夥伴經營餐廳。在截至2025年12月31日的會計年度內，中東地區開設了11家合作夥伴經營的餐廳。

headings: 與本公司品牌聲譽及餐廳營運相關之風險
食品安全及食源性疾病之憂慮可能對本公司業務產生負面影響，包括損害品牌聲譽、降低銷售額及增加成本。
若無法維持Chipotle品牌之價值與聲譽，將可能對本公司財務結果產生負面影響。
餐飲業競爭激烈。若本公司無法成功競爭，將對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生負面影響。
本公司使用第三方外送服務可能無法獲利，且若服務品質不佳，可能對本公司聲譽產生負面影響。
與人力資本相關之風險
若本公司無法聘僱、培訓並留住合資格之餐廳員工，或未能妥善規劃人力資源，將可能對本公司成長計畫及獲利能力產生負面影響。
若本公司未能遵守適用之就業及勞動法規，將可能對本公司業務產生重大且負面之影響。
勞動成本的增加，包括強制性最低工資的提高及健康福利成本的增加，可能會對本公司業務及獲利能力造成不利影響。
與網路安全、資料隱私及資訊科技系統相關的風險
本公司高度依賴資訊科技系統，若資訊科技系統發生故障或中斷，可能會影響本公司有效運作業務的能力，並可能導致顧客或員工流失。
若本公司未能完全遵守隱私權及資料保護法律及規範，可能會招致重大民事及刑事處罰與責任，並造成聲譽損害及負面宣傳。
與本公司供應鏈相關的風險
食材、餐廳設備及其他材料的成本增加，可能會對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
食材供應短缺或中斷，可能會對本公司營運結果造成不利影響。
若本公司供應鏈容量無法支持新餐廳的成長，可能會影響或延遲本公司長期成長目標的達成。
本公司有可能成為訴訟或其他法律程序的一方，這可能會對本公司業務、營運成果及聲譽產生不利影響。
與本公司成長及業務策略相關的風險
若本公司無法達成新餐廳開店目標，或無法維持現有餐廳的吸引力，則本公司利潤可能會受到影響。
本公司若無法有效管理及支援本公司成長，可能會對本公司業務及財務結果產生負面影響。
與永續性因素相關的風險
本公司需遵守不斷演進的公開披露義務，包括與永續性事項相關的部分，這可能會使本公司面臨多種風險，並可能對本公司聲譽及營運成果產生不利影響。
氣候變遷及不穩定的惡劣天氣條件可能會對本公司餐廳銷售額或營運成果產生不利影響。

paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，並配合本年度10-K表報表中其他資訊，包括「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」部分及合併財務報表與相關附註。若下列所描述的風險與不確定性發生或持續存在，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運結果，以及本公司普通股的交易價格造成重大且不利的影響。下列所描述的風險與不確定性為本公司已識別為重要的風險與不確定性，但並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險與不確定性。本公司業務亦受許多其他公司所面臨的總體經濟與產業條件等一般風險與不確定性影響。此外，尚有其他風險可能尚未為本公司所知悉，或目前認為不重要，但未來可能出現或變得重要，並可能對本公司業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運結果或普通股交易價格造成負面影響。

食品安全為本公司首要優先事項，我們投入大量資源確保本公司食品產品的安全；然而，即使從農場到餐廳的強力預防控制與幹預措施，仍無法完全消除食品安全風險。食品中毒事件已發生，且可能持續發生於本公司及其他餐廳，原因可能包括餐廳員工未正確烹調或維護食材；員工或顧客在感染傳染性疾病時進入餐廳；或因供應商、經銷商或員工未執行食品安全預防控制措施而導致食材受污染。雖然本公司監測並稽核對我們計畫的遵循情況，但我們無法保證每項食品從供應鏈起點至顧客食用過程皆能安全且正確維護。任何關於因大腸桿菌、甲型肝炎、諾羅病毒、李斯特菌、空腸彎曲桿菌、破傷風梭菌或沙門氏菌等病原體所導致的食品中毒，或其它食品安全問題，如食品篡改、污染或自然或外來物體，發生於本公司任一餐廳的報導（無論為真實或流傳），都可能對本公司聲譽造成負面影響，並對銷售造成不利影響。此外，若食品中毒事件或食品安全問題僅發生於競爭對手的餐廳或供應商或經銷商（即使本公司未與其合作），也可能導致對餐廳產業的負面宣傳，並對本公司銷售造成不利影響。食品中毒事件或食品安全問題的發生，也可能對相關食材的價格與可得性造成負面影響，進而導致成本上升與毛利率下降。

我們可能比部分競爭對手具有更高的食品安全事件風險，因為我們使用新鮮、未加工的蔬果，於餐廳中處理生雞肉，依傳統方法由員工烹調，且我們的餐點項目中不使用人工防腐劑或冷凍食材。與我們食品相關的疾病風險，也可能因我們的外送與婚宴服務業務而增加，因為我們的食品在運輸、儲存與/或供應過程中，可能不受我們控制。所有這些因素都可能對我們吸引與留住顧客的能力造成負面影響，進而可能對我們的成長與獲利造成重大負面影響。此外，美國食品供應鏈中普遍存在的化學物質與物質，如鄰苯二甲酸酯、全氟烷基物質（"PFAS"）、微塑料或重金屬，已成為增加的監管審查與對本公司及其他餐廳公司的訴訟對象，這可能會影響消費者對餐廳產業的信心，並降低餐廳銷售。

我們透過提供美味、高品質的食品，每日新鮮製作，使用負責任來源的食材，並以豐厚分量供應，建立了Chipotle品牌的強大價值。我們持續的成功取決於維持這種有吸引力的品牌價值，而這種價值可能因多種因素而受到損害，其中一些因素可能超出我們的控制範疇。可能損害我們品牌信任的事件包括實際或被認為的食品安全或食品中毒事件；員工與/或顧客被指控不道德或不專業的行為；隱私權侵害或違反隱私權法律；在餐廳內或周圍發生的安全相關事件；顧客對較小的主菜分量的觀感；或其他在本風險因素部分所描述的事件或事件。這些事件的負面影響可能因負面宣傳（包括透過社交或數位媒體）或導致訴訟而更加嚴重。社交媒體、影片分享、人脈、遊戲與訊息平台大幅增加了負面宣傳的傳播速度與範圍，往往在我們有機會調查、回應並處理問題之前。關於我們的負面線上發帖或評論，包括因不正確、虛構或惡意發帖或媒體內容所致，過去已並可能將來會放大與延長任何單一事件的負面影響，並增加對我們品牌價值的損害。
此外，若本公司、員工或商業夥伴未能遵守適用法律與規範，採取可能被視為有爭議的立場或行動，未能提供一致正面的顧客體驗，或未能建立包容與歡迎的環境，將可能導致消費者對本公司產品與品牌價值的需求顯著下降。此外，我們無法確保本公司餐廳員工或商業夥伴不會採取對本公司品牌聲譽與相關性造成負面影響的行動。

餐飲產業在味道、價格、食品品質與選擇、顧客服務、品牌聲譽、數位參與、廣告與促銷活動，以及餐廳的地理位置、吸引力與維護等方面具有高度競爭性。我們也與非傳統市場參與者競爭，例如以套餐形式出現的便利餐點，如超市提供的主菜、配菜或餐點組合套件，餐點組合配送服務，以及「幽靈」或「暗廚」餐廳，即餐點在獨立的外帶場所準備而非餐廳內。配送聚合商與食品配送服務，為消費者提供廣泛競爭餐廳連鎖與食品零售商的便利存取，尤其在都市化地區，可能根據付費置頂、線上評論等因素，將潛在顧客導向其他餐廳，並可能與我們的顧客建立更緊密的關係。競爭的增加可能對我們的銷售、獲利與發展計畫造成負面影響。若顧客的口味或飲食偏好改變，若我們的行銷努力失敗，或若我們無法成功與其他餐飲概念競爭，將可能對我們的業務造成負面影響。
